decision: require repeated benchmark stability evidence before using rollback timings to choose exact snapshot versus mutation-delta rollback

reviews.correctness: A single p95 run can be distorted by scheduler, GC, filesystem, or CPU noise. Compare repeated runs at identical queue sizes before treating timing as design evidence.
reviews.robustness_security: Fail closed on missing, malformed, or incomparable benchmark runs. Do not weaken rollback invariants or persistence fencing to improve timing.
reviews.latency_resources_regression: Use an offline relative-spread check over existing benchmark results. It adds no worker, Qubes, network, or production runtime overhead and avoids a higher-risk mutation-delta rewrite based on noisy data.

winner: repeatability gate over existing failure-path benchmark results

alternatives.rejected: too sensitive to runtime noise to justify a production rollback redesign
larger state-equivalence and regression surface without stable evidence of a bottleneck
adds infrastructure and provenance complexity before Slice 1 has independent CI

qa: Require at least two comparable runs, identical queue-size sets, finite non-negative p95 measurements, and relative p95 spread <= 25% for failed enqueue and failed claim at every measured queue size.
lesson: Performance evidence should be reproducible before it is allowed to drive a correctness-sensitive rollback implementation change.
